strengths: Strong empirical results with 2.53× F1 improvement over strongest baseline consistently across 8 diverse benchmarks, with balanced performance (F1 ≈ accuracy vs. baseline gaps)
Rigorous experimental protocol using subject hold-out validation preventing data leakage and testing true user generalization
Comprehensive ablation studies systematically demonstrating necessity of knowledge base, retrieval, and pruning components with detailed per-dataset analysis
Valuable interpretability contribution: generates verifiable natural language explanations grounded in selected features and retrieved evidence, important for safety-critical applications
Clever technical design: pair-wise knowledge base label-agnostic, class-wise retrieval prevents long-tail bias, two-stage feature selection progressively focuses reasoning
Thorough documentation with complete prompts, dataset details, per-class results, and baseline specifications supporting reproducibility
Practical zero-shot framework without task-specific fine-tuning, achieving true classifier-free generalization at test time
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines existing components (AutoGluon feature importance, reciprocal rank fusion from IR, multi-step LLM prompting) with incremental engineering contribution rather than fundamental methodological advance

Overstated 'zero-shot' claims: requires labeled training data from seen subjects for knowledge base construction; evaluated only on held-out users from same dataset/activity classes, not entirely new activities or cross-dataset scenarios

Insufficient failure analysis: per-class results show severe failures (USC-HAD elevators at 30%, WISDM eating sandwich at 6.2%) with no investigation of root causes (knowledge base, retrieval, or reasoning deficiency)

Handcrafted feature engineering creates brittleness: 64+ manually designed features (Table 8) require dataset-specific window sizes/sampling rates; limited justification for choices; no sensitivity analysis to feature quality degradation

Computational cost and scalability unaddressed: multiple LLM API calls per inference with no token usage/cost breakdown, O(|A|²) pairwise knowledge base scaling, no analysis of performance with 50+ activities or cross-dataset scalability

Experimental setup limitations: inference subsets sampled for cost (non-representative), cross-dataset evaluation entirely missing, open-set evaluation (WISDM/DSADS) only retrieves top-10 classes not arbitrary activities, knowledge base and test activities overlap (same distribution)

Missing ablation studies: no analysis of knowledge base training data requirements, degraded knowledge bases, combined ablations (-knowledge -retrieval), or individual component contribution breakdowns
Hyperparameter justification absent: RRF k_rrf=60, retrieval k=100, feature selection parameters n/m unchosen systematically; no sensitivity analyses or principled justification provided

Retrieval analysis incomplete: Figure 5 confirms retrieval importance but lacks precision/recall metrics, relevance analysis, or explanation of why retrieval helps more on some datasets (PAMAP2 -18.8%) vs. others (Opportunity -8.5%)

Statistical rigor concerns: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or multiple runs reported; small test sets (DSADS 10 samples/activity); upper bound variance (71-99.6%) unexplained; random seed effects unaddressed

Prompting robustness unvalidated: heavy dependence on carefully crafted system prompts with no ablation on variations; temperature=0 ensures reproducibility but limits reasoning flexibility; transferability to different LLMs unclear

Domain specificity limits impact: HAR with motion sensors is niche for ACL venue (better suited to UBICOMP/IoT conferences); insights unlikely to transfer to other time-series domains; requires LLM API access limiting offline applicability

strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 8 HAR benchmarks with proper subject-held-out protocol and consistent strong performance improvements (2.53× macro F1 over strongest baseline)
Thorough ablation studies validating the necessity of each component (retrieval, pruning agent, prior knowledge)
Well-detailed implementation with full prompts, features, and preprocessing steps in appendix
Interpretable predictions grounded in selected features and retrieved evidence, moving beyond black-box decisions
Solid technical execution combining domain knowledge, retrieval, and hierarchical agent reasoning
weaknesses: Critical scope mismatch: This is fundamentally a sensor/ubiquitous computing paper (motion time-series analysis), not NLP. While it uses LLMs, the core contribution is in HAR signal analysis, not language processing. Should be submitted to Ubicomp, MobiSys, or ISWC instead of ACL

Severely misleading 'zero-shot' framing: The method requires labeled training data to construct the knowledge base and embeddings. This is cross-subject generalization within the same dataset, not true zero-shot learning. No evaluation on completely novel activities unseen during infrastructure construction

Heavy dependency on handcrafted features undermines 'plug-and-play' claims: The 50+ manually-designed features are accelerometer/gyroscope-specific. Deploying to different sensor types would require entirely new feature sets

Incremental technical novelty: Each component (handcrafted features, RAG retrieval, agent-based prompting with LLMs) is well-established. The contribution is primarily an engineering combination rather than fundamental innovation

Experimental scope limitations: (1) Only within-dataset cross-subject evaluation; (2) No cross-dataset or cross-sensor evaluation; (3) No evaluation on held-out activity classes; (4) LLM baselines given raw data (unfairly weak); (5) Unfair comparison with frozen foundation models

Infrastructure scalability concerns: For M activities, requires O(M²) pairwise profiles. Adding activities requires recomputing importance scores against all existing activities, not the claimed O(|F|) updates
Unvalidated interpretability claims: Explanations are template-generated by LLM prompting, not learned. No human evaluation of explanation quality, correctness, or trustworthiness

Missing critical analyses: No error analysis or failure mode discussion; extreme per-class disparities (Figure 8: 18.8%-100%) unexplained; no sensitivity to hyperparameters (k=100, k_rrf=60); missing ablation on feature set design
Misleading 'Classifier-Free Generalization' terminology obscures that the approach still depends on labeled training data for knowledge base and retrieval database construction
No end-to-end inference latency reported with LLM API calls; reproducibility concerns with external API dependency (Gemini 2.0-Flash), unclear hyperparameter sensitivity

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 diverse datasets with 10 different baselines, demonstrating consistent 2.53× macro F1 improvement and rigorous subject-hold-out protocol ensuring genuine zero-shot generalization
Convincing ablation studies showing substantial performance drops from removing each component (retrieval: -10%, pruning: -13%, knowledge: -18%), conclusively proving necessity of each module

Novel interpretability contribution: generates verifiable natural language explanations grounded in selected features and retrieved evidence, substantially advancing trust and explainability over black-box baselines
Elegant pairwise knowledge base design achieving O(|F|) complexity for new activities (vs. retraining), enabling true plug-and-play zero-shot generalization without task-specific adaptation

Sound technical architecture: hierarchical agent pipeline with coarse-to-fine reasoning is intuitive; class-wise multi-sensor retrieval with RRF prevents single-sensor bias; placement-specific databases are practical
Strong practical value for real-world HAR: addresses genuine limitations of existing methods regarding generalization to new sensors and activities without costly retraining
Excellent reproducibility: complete prompt templates, detailed dataset descriptions, code promised, deterministic inference with temperature=0, and extensive ablations/per-class results provided
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: statistical feature extraction, RRF ranking fusion, and LLM prompting are all well-established; primary contribution is architectural combination rather than algorithmic innovation

Substantial performance gap to foundation models with classifiers (Table 2): ZARA achieves 81.6% vs. Mantis+classifier at 90.5% (8.9% absolute difference), suggesting inherent limitations of the knowledge/retrieval paradigm that deserve deeper analysis

Production deployment costs completely unaddressed: relies on proprietary Gemini 2.0-Flash API (licensing, rate limits, reliability), but paper reports only retrieval latency, not total inference time including LLM calls—critical gap for real-world adoption

Insufficient failure mode analysis: Figure 8 shows severe per-class variation (e.g., 6.2% for Eating Sandwich, 30% for Elevator Down) with no investigation of causes, error patterns, or systematic weaknesses
Knowledge base construction under-justified: uses AutoGluon permutation-based importance without exploring alternatives (SHAP, Gini, MI) or validating robustness to database sampling variations

Hyperparameter choices under-explored: k=100 default (top-k), N/M feature counts tied to heuristics, but no ablations or sensitivity analyses; Table 6 suggests k=100 may be suboptimal for some datasets

Baseline evaluation concerns: ImageBind/IMU2CLIP evaluated via 'best placement' selection when these are inherently single-sensor methods—multi-sensor fusion could strengthen these baselines; IMUGPT excluded from some analyses reducing consistency

Knowledge base scalability unaddressed: O(activity_pairs) storage burden (500K pairs for 1K activities) not analyzed; unclear how this compares computationally/memory-wise to training compact classifiers

Limited activity diversity: all activities are coarse-grained standard behaviors (walking, sitting); no evaluation on fine-grained distinctions (eating types), domain-specific skills, or complex sequences limiting generalization claims

Pruning safety concern: upper bound accuracy of 91.4% indicates correct class removed ~8.6% of time—concerning for safety-critical applications (healthcare, worker safety) but not analyzed or discussed

strengths: Well-motivated approach that elegantly addresses the gap between sensor time-series and LLM reasoning by translating implicit signal patterns into verifiable linguistic priors
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 datasets with rigorous subject-hold-out protocol, two-tier evaluation design, and comparison against 10 diverse baselines
Consistent improvements across all benchmarks and multiple LLM backbones (Qwen-30B/80B, GPT, Gemini), demonstrating generalizability of the approach
Excellent reproducibility documentation including full prompts, detailed preprocessing, feature specifications, and baseline implementation details
Thorough ablation studies convincingly demonstrate necessity of each component (retrieval, pruning, knowledge injection)
Provides interpretable predictions with human-readable explanations grounded in retrieved evidence, addressing trust concerns in safety-critical HAR applications
weaknesses: Baseline selection concerns: direct prompting methods perform surprisingly poorly (10-25%), and single-sensor baselines evaluated on multi-sensor data introduce fairness issues. The very large gaps (81.6% vs 39.4%) may partially reflect weak baselines rather than method strength

Cross-dataset generalization is mixed: in-dataset knowledge outperforms cross-dataset knowledge in 5/8 cases, and cross-dataset knowledge underperforms 'No Knowledge' baseline in 3 cases, contradicting claims of robust transfer

Overstated positioning: claims of 'training-free' and 'plug-and-play' are misleading—requires labeled retrieval database, costly preprocessing, and pairwise feature recomputation when adding activities
Hand-crafted feature engineering (Table 10 lists 60+ features) contradicts claims of automation; requires significant domain expertise and no exploration of simpler feature sets
Lacks human evaluation of interpretability claims despite identifying transparency as a key contribution; no validation that explanations are actually useful or correct
No statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or variance analysis across runs; cross-dataset results reported as point estimates
Limited methodological novelty: components (permutation importance, RRF fusion, hierarchical LLM reasoning) are known techniques; novelty is primarily in application
Insufficient detail on design choices: k_rrf=60 not ablated, feature selection heuristics informal, cross-validation procedure for feature importance not fully specified

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 HAR datasets with rigorous subject-holdout protocol and 10 diverse baselines
Strong empirical results showing substantial improvements (81.6% average accuracy vs 39.4% for best baseline UniMTS)
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating that all components (retrieval, knowledge, pruning) contribute to performance
Excellent reproducibility with detailed implementation details, token usage analysis, per-class results, full prompts, and promised code release
Generates interpretable natural-language explanations for predictions grounded in statistical evidence
weaknesses: Fundamental scope mismatch: This is a domain-specific HAR application paper, not a computational linguistics contribution. LLMs serve as a templated reasoning engine rather than advancing NLP or LLM science

Misleading 'training-free' framing: The method requires labeled data to construct knowledge bases and retrieval databases. While not updating parameters, this provides significant adaptation advantage not equally available to baselines—fair comparison is compromised

Limited methodological novelty: Combines standard techniques (handcrafted feature extraction, permutation-based importance ranking, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, hierarchical prompting), each well-established; the combination is incremental

Domain-specific feature engineering (Table 10: 30+ hand-designed features) contradicts 'plug-and-play' claims. Different domains require entirely different feature sets, undermining generalizability and making this a form of hidden domain adaptation

Cross-dataset transfer results contradict generalization claims: In-dataset knowledge outperforms cross-dataset knowledge in 5/8 cases (Figure 5). Post-hoc explanations about user diversity are unconvincing

Insufficient novelty analysis: Ablations show all components matter but don't explain why ZARA vastly outperforms baselines. Alternative hypothesis—that labeled adaptation data provides sufficient advantage regardless of reasoning mechanism—is not ruled out

Unfair baseline treatment: UniMTS and others don't access the same labeled adaptation data (knowledge base + retrieval database) in the same way, making direct comparison invalid without supervised baseline controls
Poor performance on many activities undermines robustness (Figure 9): Some classes achieve 6-50% accuracy (e.g., MHealth jogging 30%, WISDM eating activities 6-37%). No error analysis provided
Overstated interpretability claims: Generated explanations are template-based statistical comparisons, not deep reasoning about decisions. This is feature attribution, not true interpretability
Computational cost underexplored: Multi-stage agent pipeline requires multiple LLM API calls. Cost-accuracy tradeoffs and practical deployment feasibility inadequately addressed

strengths: Novel and well-motivated core insight: Statistically-grounded textual knowledge injection elegantly bridges the signal-to-language gap for LLM application to sensor data, addressing a genuine technical challenge

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 8 datasets, 10 baselines across three method families, rigorous Subject-Hold-Out protocol, both cross-subject and cross-dataset evaluation with large performance gaps (81.6% vs 39.4% for UniMTS)
Thorough ablation studies with upper-bound metrics: Each component's necessity quantified (Retrieval: -10%, Pruning: -13%, Knowledge: -18%), providing clear evidence of soundness
Exceptional reproducibility: Full prompts, preprocessing details, baseline implementations, per-class results, feature specifications, and token usage transparently provided
Interpretability and practical value: Human-readable explanations grounded in evidence; parameter-frozen inference enables deployment without task-specific training
Interesting cross-dataset transfer findings: Counter-intuitive result that cross-dataset knowledge can outperform in-dataset knowledge, with insights about user diversity and data density effects
weaknesses: Narrow domain scope: Motion sensor HAR only; applicability to other sensor modalities or time-series domains unclear, limiting generalizability and ACL relevance
Requires labeled target-domain support data: Despite 'training-free' framing, still needs labeled retrieval database from target domain, contradicting true zero-shot claims

Substantial LLM model dependency: 10.6% performance variance across models (Qwen-30B: 71.0% to Gemini: 81.6%); results depend on numerical reasoning ability and may not generalize as LLM capabilities evolve

Knowledge base construction not fully justified: Permutation importance method not compared to alternatives (SHAP, etc.); handcrafted features (40+) unexplored against learned approaches; pairwise formulation lacks justification
Weak theoretical understanding of transfer: 'User diversity' and 'data density' explanations are post-hoc without formal analysis; only 4 transfer pairs tested, limiting generalization claims
Performance ceiling on harder tasks: Significant drops (USC-HAD: 60%, WISDM: 65.6%); weaker on multi-sensor/high-channel datasets raise practical applicability concerns
Small held-out subject counts: Opportunity (1 subject), Shoaib (2 subjects) and randomly sampled inference subsets limit statistical rigor; no confidence intervals or significance tests reported
Limited methodological novelty: Feature importance, retrieval, and LLM prompting are well-established; main contribution is their combination for HAR rather than novel components
